messages.text: Our office espresso machine is leaking. A wants a simpler one and B wants to keep the old one. I don't want a fight over coffee. Can you help us sort it out?
I mostly just want working coffee again without this turning into a fight. The leak is messy, but I’m not sure it makes the machine unusable. I can’t take on coordinating the repair myself.

I can see why the old one matters, especially since it was Dad’s. I’d just lean toward something simpler and reliable, with less cleaning and upkeep—I’m pretty worn out after work and can’t take on a repair or rota.
I want it repaired and kept. It was our dad’s, and keeping it going feels personal to me. But it keeps breaking, and I don’t have much time for a drawn-out repair process.
Yes, that’s about right. I’d just say I don’t want to be the one chasing everyone to make it happen.
Mostly, yes—I’d like something reliable that doesn’t add upkeep to my plate. I understand Dad’s machine matters to B, though I wouldn’t say the sentimental value is mine in the same way.
Mostly. It matters because it was Dad’s, and I want it repaired and kept. I just can’t take on a drawn-out process; it needs to fit into small chunks of time.
Option 1 seems simplest, if A or B handles the booking and everyone agrees. Someone else scheduling would address my concern. I don’t know what the repair would cost.
Option 3 sounds closest to what I’d want, if B is comfortable with it. I’d just need someone else to handle the arrangements—I can’t take on coordinating repairs or a long back-and-forth.

Option 1 is closest, if it really takes just a small chunk of my time. Option 2 might work if Dad’s machine is still repaired and kept, but I’m not sure about adding another machine. Option 3 doesn’t fit—keeping it as a display piece isn’t the same as keeping it going.

That would be manageable for me if I’m not expected to coordinate or take on upkeep afterward. I’d still prefer a simpler machine long term, since I’m not sure a repair will keep the old one reliable.

Yes, I’m open to revisiting if it breaks again; I’m not agreeing to endless repairs. If A books it and the visit can fit a small time slot, that works for me. The scheduling could still be a hassle if I have to coordinate it or wait around.
Nothing else from me. Please confirm A is comfortable and the cost is agreed before anyone books; I’m still not able to coordinate it.

I’m afraid I can’t take on booking the repair—that’s the coordinating I said I don’t have capacity for. I’m comfortable with the repair plan if someone else can arrange it and we agree on the cost first.
That’s okay, as long as we agree on the cost first and I’m not left coordinating or waiting around for the service call. I’m still only agreeing to this repair, not endless repairs.
A third-party service sounds reasonable, but I can’t make the call or coordinate it. Someone else will need to take that on.
